\section[indagare]{indagare — to investigate}

\label{lesson:IT-C295-indagare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the video camera, then the Italian for the chase.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: indagare}
\textbf{indagare} — \textquotedblleft{}to investigate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La polizia indaga sulla rapina.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The police are investigating the robbery.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Indagare su} qualcosa.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{indagare} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{indāgāre} \textquotedblleft{}to track down\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), first said of hunting dogs; EtymDB links it with \emph{indāgō} \textquotedblleft{}a ring of hunters\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indagare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{indagare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{indagare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the video camera, then the Italian for the chase, then say \emph{indagare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does indagare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To investigate\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[l'indagine]{l'indagine — the police investigation, the inquiry}

\label{lesson:IT-C295-indagine}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the chase, then the Italian for to investigate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'indagine}
\textbf{l'indagine} — \textquotedblleft{}the police investigation, the inquiry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'indagine è durata due anni.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The investigation lasted two years.}
\end{quote}

Often plural: \emph{le indagini continuano}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{indagine} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{indāgō} \textquotedblleft{}a ring of hunters, a search\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the chase, then the Italian for to investigate, then say \emph{l'indagine} again

\section[l'ispettore]{l'ispettore — the inspector}

\label{lesson:IT-C295-ispettore}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to investigate, then the Italian for the police investigation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'ispettore}
\textbf{l'ispettore} — \textquotedblleft{}the inspector\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
L'ispettore ha parlato con tutti i vicini.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The inspector spoke to all the neighbours.}
\end{quote}

A woman is \emph{l'ispettrice}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ispettore} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{īnspector} \textquotedblleft{}an examiner\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{īnspicere} \textquotedblleft{}to look into\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to investigate, then the Italian for the police investigation, then say \emph{l'ispettore} again

\section[l'indizio]{l'indizio — the clue}

\label{lesson:IT-C295-indizio}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the police investigation, then the Italian for the inspector.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'indizio}
\textbf{l'indizio} — \textquotedblleft{}the clue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Non ci sono indizi: il caso è difficile.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There are no clues: the case is a hard one.}
\end{quote}

Detective stories live on \emph{indizi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{indizio} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{indicium} \textquotedblleft{}a sign, a mark\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{index} \textquotedblleft{}one who points out\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{l'indizio}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{l'indizio}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the police investigation, then the Italian for the inspector, then say \emph{l'indizio} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does l'indizio mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The clue\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[l'impronta]{l'impronta — the footprint; the fingerprint}

\label{lesson:IT-C295-impronta}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the inspector, then the Italian for the clue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'impronta}
\textbf{l'impronta} — \textquotedblleft{}the footprint; the fingerprint\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Sulla neve ci sono impronte di scarpe.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There are shoe prints in the snow.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Le impronte digitali} — fingerprints.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{impronta} is built on \emph{improntare} \textquotedblleft{}to stamp, to press a mark into\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB); where \emph{improntare} comes from is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
